So, you travel a lot. Do you have children?
Yes, two. A son and a daughter.
How old are they?
My son is fourteen and he plays football. My daughter is nineteen and she studies.
Does she live with you?
No, she lives in another city. My son still lives with us.
And your wife? Does she travel with you?
No, she stays at home. She goes to the market every Saturday and talks to everybody there.
That sounds nice. And what do you do at the weekend, when you are at home?
We are together, the four of us, and we do something simple. And you? Do you have children?
One. He is six, and he asks four hundred questions a day. Every day.

We live in Sao Paulo and I travel a lot.
But tell me about you. Do you have children?

You asked about my family, so here they are, quickly. My husband is a teacher. He works at a school ten minutes from our house, and he walks there every day, in the rain, in the sun, always. My daughter is nineteen and she studies medicine in another city, so we only see her at the weekend, and not every weekend. My son is fourteen and he lives with us. He plays football, badly, and he tells me it is the referee's fault, always. And the dog. The dog does nothing, and he is the only one of us who is never tired. That is my family. Now tell me about yours.

People ask me what we do at the weekend, and the honest answer is: not much, and that is the idea. On Saturday morning my wife goes to the market, always the same one, and she takes an hour to buy four things because she talks to everybody there. I stay at home with the children. In the afternoon we are together, the four of us, and we do something simple. My son wants the beach every time. My daughter wants the cinema every time. So we go to the beach one week and to the cinema the next week, and nobody is happy, and everybody comes. On Sunday we do nothing at all. That is my favourite part.
